name: exported_cases
source: WHO DON 2026-DON602, 2026-DON603, and WHO Director-General Ministerial Briefing 25 May 2026 — three travel-related (DRC) cases imported into Uganda: (i) elderly man admitted Kampala 11 May 2026, died 14 May; (ii) second import confirmed 16 May 2026 in Kampala with no apparent link to the first; (iii) woman from DRC who travelled Arua to Entebbe to Kampala with mild symptoms, tested positive on follow-up, announced 23 May 2026 (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/5/23/uganda-confirms-three-new-ebola-cases-bringing-total-to-five). Two additional Uganda confirmed cases announced 23 May (a driver and a healthcare worker) are domestic contacts of import #1 and are excluded — this model treats Uganda as imports only.

name: exports_deaths
source: WHO DON 2026-DON602 — one death (import #1, died 14 May 2026). No deaths reported among imports #2 or #3 as of the 28 May 2026 cut-off. The exports count is the cumulative detected by the cut-off: a 4th Uganda travel-linked case appears in 2-June reporting but is detected after 28 May, so it is not counted here.

name: first_export_detection_date
source: WHO DON 2026-DON602 — import #1 hospital-admitted 11 May 2026 (point-of-entry/hospital detection date). Used as a one-sided timing bound on T. Detection dates for imports #2 (confirmed 16 May) and #3 (announced 23 May; underlying detection date not published) are not used by the model: only the earliest detection enters the timing term.

name: export_case_dates
source: WHO DON 2026-DON602, 2026-DON603, and WHO Director-General Ministerial Briefing 25 May 2026 — Uganda report dates of the three travel-related imports: #1 hospital-admitted Kampala 11 May 2026; #2 confirmed Kampala 16 May 2026; #3 (Arua-Entebbe-Kampala traveller) announced 23 May 2026. Loaded as a daily detection series and fitted with the dated export-case likelihood (per-day Poisson). #1 and #2 are detection/confirmation dates; #3 is the public announcement date (the underlying detection date was not published), so it carries report-pipeline lag. Matches the count in [exported_cases].

name: export_death_dates
source: WHO DON 2026-DON602 — the fatal Uganda export (import #1) was hospital-admitted 11 May 2026 and died 14 May 2026 (hospital-recorded death date). A list of dated export deaths; loaded as a daily series and fitted with a binned-Poisson likelihood that bounds T.

name: total_deaths

Frozen at this 26 May value, two days before the 28 May cut-off: INSP stopped publishing a national suspected-death total from 28 May. Recorded in data/insp_sitrep_scanned.csv.

name: reported_cases
source: INSP SitRep 012 (data as of 26 May 2026), front-page `Cumul cas suspects`, read from the situation-report PDF. National cumulative suspected cases; recorded in data/insp_sitrep_scanned.csv. This report carries no per-zone case table, so the headline could not be cross-checked against a zone-row sum. Frozen at this 26 May value, two days before the 28 May cut-off: INSP began revising the suspected count downward from 27 May (906, then 349) as suspects were reclassified.

name: occupancy_break_dates
source: Occupancy reclassification-break days: documented, non-confounded between-report basis changes in isolation_history where the reported start-of-day in-bed stock (Patients au lit (J-1)) falls below the previous report's end-of-day occupancy (Patients en isolement Fin J) by more than the day's admissions and discharges can bridge, a reclassification the smooth inflow-through-survival demand cannot reproduce. Both fall on consecutive published SitReps (no intervening unpublished vintage), so each is a clean one-day step rather than a two-day increment confounded with growth. 2026-06-09: the Fin J occupancy steps 8 June 297 -> 9 June 260 (-37) during a growing outbreak, and the 9 June start-of-day au-lit (J-1) 268 (SitRep 026 isolement table Ituri 245 + Nord-Kivu 17 + Sud-Kivu 6 = 268) is -29 below the 8 June Fin J 297 (SitRep 025), against near-exact reconciliation on the neighbouring days (7 June au-lit 283 vs 6 June Fin J 283 = 0; 8 June 310 vs 7 June 309 = +1; 10 June 262 vs 9 June 260 = +2). The drop is concentrated in the suspected pool: dont suspects 184 (SitRep 025, 8 June) -> 143 (SitRep 026, 9 June) = -41 while dont confirmes 113 -> 117 = +4, a de-registration of ruled-out suspects, not a fall in confirmed cases. It coincides with the first Taux d'occupation print (65.0% on 9 June) and a SitRep 026 mission conjointe surveillance / prise en charge pour evaluer la capacite d'isolement, an isolation-register review; SitReps 024-026 (7-9 June) are consecutive and published, so the 8 -> 9 June step is clean. The au-lit stock is read from SitRep 026 directly because treatment_aulit_history begins 13 June (Tableau 6), so the 9 June break is not corroborated by that block but by the isolement table in the report itself. 2026-06-19: the occupancy (Fin J) steps 18 June 416 -> 19 June 361, and the 19 June Tableau 6 start-of-day stock au-lit (J-1) 342 confirms a -74 reclassification against the 18 June Fin J 416 (treatment_aulit_history), the largest au-lit-vs-previous-Fin-J gap in the series. The 27 and 29 June steps (419 -> 502 -> 609) each cross an unpublished SitRep (043 on 26 June, 045 on 28 June), so they are two-day increments confounded with real growth rather than a clean reclassification and are left out. 2026-07-14: the 14 July start-of-day au-lit (J-1) 694 (SitRep 061 Tableau 6 Ituri 541 + Nord-Kivu 149 + Tshopo 4) is -59 below the 13 July Fin J 753 (SitRep 060), a clean one-day step (SitReps 059/060/061 are consecutive published vintages) comparable to the 19 June -74. The drop is concentrated in the suspected pool (dont suspects 507 -> 466 = -41 while dont confirmes 246 -> 270 = +24), the de-registration signature, not a fall in confirmed cases. 2026-08-11: added on @seabbs's explicit direction (PR #567 review) after the national trend (per data/README.md and issue #562 item 3) showed the 10 -> 11 August step (Fin J 716 -> 570, -146) as a break rather than in-range noise. No au-lit (J-1) figure exists to corroborate mechanically the brief MVEBDB format carries no Tableau 6 (frozen since SitRep 080; issue #562) - so this break, unlike the three above, rests on the maintainer's read of the national series rather than an au-lit-vs-Fin-J reconciliation. Context (see issue #562 comment on PR #567 for the full arithmetic): decomposing the national tile into Ituri's own separately-stated occupancy and the implied non-Ituri remainder gives 221/196/299/195 for 8-11 August, so the remainder is not itself obviously trending down into 11 August (that reading would instead flag 10 August, 299, as the outlier). 11 August is also the first vintage in this format where Nord-Kivu discloses a current stock at all (176, worded 'malades en hospitalisation'), so an alternative account is a same-day definitional broadening rather than a discharge event, but this could not be resolved from the PDFs alone; the maintainer's break-day call stands regardless of which mechanism is correct, since occupancy_break_dates absorbs the discontinuity either way.

name: confirmed_break_dates
source: Retrospective harmonisation-break days for confirmed_case_history / confirmed_death_history: days whose cumulative headline step is acknowledged by the report itself to be mostly a provincial base integration rather than 24h notifications. 2026-07-22 (SitRep 069): the page-1 headline is asterisked `Harmonisation de donnees avec les provinces de l'Ituri et du Nord-Kivu a la date du 22 juillet 2026`, and the report states explicitly that `les augmentations importantes observees dans les cumuls resultent principalement de l'integration des bases provinciales harmonisees et ne refletent pas uniquement les nouvelles notifications des dernieres 24 heures`. The cumulative confirmed steps +369 (2536 -> 2905) against a printed 24h new-confirmed count of +97 (Ituri 73, Nord-Kivu 18, Haut-Uele 6), and confirmed deaths +236 (1033 -> 1269) against +62 gross. Three independent checks agree the step is retrospective rather than real incidence: the Tableau 6 in-care death outflow that day is only 32; the confirmed-in-care stock barely moves (274 -> 285) while the cumulative gains 369; and SitRep 070 the next day returns to +68 gross = +68 net, so it is a one-day event and not a level shift in incidence. Without the break day the 24h analysed denominator published for 22 July (414) pairs with the +369 increment in the laboratory positivity likelihood, giving an implied 89,1% positivity against the 23,4% (97/414) actually reported - the most extreme observation in the positivity series, and almost entirely artefact. Note the existing inclusion rule (confirmed increment <= analysed) PASSED this day with 45 to spare: that rule guards against an impossible denominator, not a harmonisation, so it offers no protection here. SitRep 065 (18 July) is the other known harmonisation (Haut-Uele/Nia-Nia reattachment) but is NOT listed, and the bar is stated for BOTH streams because a break day applies to cases and deaths alike: +83 gross vs +77 net cases and +40 gross vs +37 net deaths. Both net steps are SMALLER than their gross 24h counts, so the increment likelihood is if anything under-fed rather than over-fed, and both discrepancies (6 cases, 3 deaths) are well inside the surveillance dispersion. The two streams moving down together is what a transfer between provinces looks like (Haut-Uele's provincial cumulative was revised to 16 cases and 10 deaths) rather than a base integration, which adds to both. Added per issue #484. `gross_cases` and `gross_deaths` are the PRINTED 24h new-confirmed counts on each break day (page-1 tile: 22 July +97 cases = Ituri 73 + Nord-Kivu 18 + Haut-Uele 6, and +62 deces = Ituri 45 + Nord-Kivu 14 + Haut-Uele 3). They make the fitted step DATA-DERIVED rather than a guessed prior width: the model centres each step on the observed discrepancy (the vintage increment minus the printed gross count, so 369 - 97 = 272 cases and 236 - 62 = 174 deaths on 22 July) and samples around it with `confirmed_break_sd`, which is now only the residual uncertainty about how much of that discrepancy is truly retrospective rather than coincident same-day incidence - not the magnitude of the harmonisation itself, which the report publishes. Both arrays must be the same length as `value` and are filtered to the cut-off with it.

name: genetic_tmrca
source: BEAST X v10.6.0 analysis of 139 BDBV genomes (mbalaplacide2026, 2026-07-10 virological.org post; GTR substitution model, strict molecular clock, Skygrid and Exponential growth coalescent priors). Skygrid baseline: mean TMRCA 2026-03-15, 95% HPD 2026-02-09 to 2026-04-12. Exponential growth sensitivity: mean TMRCA 2026-03-08, 95% HPD 2026-02-01 to 2026-04-05. Both at the outbreak-specific ~1.1E-3 substitutions/site/year rate. Estimates sample 139 genomes across 16 health zones and are a lower bound on the outbreak age, since further sequencing only pushes the TMRCA older. Using the genetic TMRCA as a seeding bound follows a suggestion of N. Ferguson (ferguson2026).
